findings.text: The reviewed run recorded no baseline_suite arm in its manifest (head-only gate), so its record alone cannot show the change added no failures. This review supplied the base arm against a git-archive export of 1e44c348 and found the scratch base arm red for a reason that is not a pre-existing baseline: the shared store under /work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa/machine_description was re-converted by the node, so the base catalogue's placeholders no longer name its emitted elements. The head arm is green (56 passed, EXIT=0). Recorded so the next arm-required implement node emits both arms, not as a defect of the change.

The SPEC's done-when requires a test asserting that no element identifier in jt-60sa.json ends in a slash, which is catalogue-wide, so satisfying it also required naming the pf_passive vessel filaments (VV1_1..VV1_63, VV2_1..VV2_57, OP2 VV1_1..VV1_98) in build_pf_passive, one line beyond the pf_active goal. The node discloses this in evidence_inputs/follow_ons. It is a required consequence of the spec's global test rather than unrequested creep, and the catalogue now carries real names for all three vessel loops; recorded so a coordinator can confirm the extension is wanted.

follow_ons: The reviewed run's manifest carries no baseline_suite arm; a coordinator wanting an arm-derived added-failure figure for an implement node should have the node record both arms.

The pf_passive vessel-filament naming (VV1_*/VV2_*) extends beyond the pf_active goal to satisfy the catalogue-wide no-trailing-slash test; if unwanted, the catalogue test would need scoping to pf_active assemblies and the store re-converted.
The section 4 probe-angle binding item (magnetics/b_field_pol_probe/poloidal_angle) remains untouched and open, as the node states.

justifications: Independent review of run r-20261006T054914831371-jtmm-coil-element-names (plan imas-ambix:jt60sa-machine-map section 4), reviewed_base_sha 1e44c3488e12f4e8c04fab0dd5d04f75ac736dc3, reviewed_head_sha 12986e9dfdb63bf7fcbd83799c76fbc7701cb7d9, stored as a parsed record scoring all six dimensions in 0..20 -- goal_fidelity 20, evidence 19, scope_discipline 20, durability 19, fit 20, reuse 20 -- total 118 in the 0..120 sum. Goal fidelity is full: build_pf_active names every coil element {coil}_{position} and the catalogue carries the store's real names; I read both phases' pf_active.nc read-only at DD 4.1.1 and found 12 coils, 268 elements, 0 unnamed (CS1_1..CS1_40, EF1_1..EF1_16, FPPC_UP_1..6), matching the store receipts that name converter commit 81998115. Evidence is strong but not full: the reviewed run's head gate reproduces exactly (56 passed, EXIT=0) and the declared negative control reproduces (removing the build_pf_active name assignment reddens the coil-element test, EXIT=1), but the reviewed manifest recorded no baseline_suite arm, so its record alone cannot show the change added no failures; my scratch base arm is red only because the shared store had moved with the head (the placeholders no longer name emitted elements), not from a pre-existing baseline. Scope is full: the diff is exactly the five granted files (1472/1290) with no plan or figure edit and a clean worktree; the catalogue edit is line-by-line (563 hunks, all identifier lines), not a re-serialisation. Durability is strong: the new test asserts names in deck order and uniqueness within the coil, the negative control shows it fires, and the geometry adapter enforces identifier-to-element agreement end to end. Fit is full: the change is one naming line per builder, an __all__ declaration and a data-file identifier replacement, adding no engine code and no machine-name branch. Reuse is full: it extends the existing converter and catalogue rather than reimplementing anything. Two follow-on findings are recorded (the absent baseline arm, and the pf_passive vessel-filament naming that the spec's global no-trailing-slash test required beyond the pf_active goal); neither blocks landing.
